coverage_notes: A04 Insecure Design is largely architectural and is treated as out of scope for this prototype. A10 SSRF is not claimed for this catalog.

findings.title: Search input is not safely parameterised
findings.description: The product search path concatenates user-controlled input into a database query. On a deliberately vulnerable training app this is a known injection class: untrusted input can change query meaning.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding for OWASP Juice Shop. Live checks in this demo do not send attack payloads; they only confirm the target is reachable and inspect response headers.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterised queries or an ORM for every data store call. Validate search terms against an allow-list of expected characters and return generic errors.

findings.title: Reflected script execution in search results
findings.description: Search terms are reflected into the page without context-aware encoding. That is the classic stored/reflected XSS pattern taught by Juice Shop.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. No exploit string is used or stored by WebSET.
findings.recommendation: Encode all untrusted output for the HTML/JS context it is inserted into. Prefer a templating library that encodes by default, and add a strict Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: Administrative functions reachable without a matching authorisation check
findings.description: Several administration-style routes exist on the client and API. Visibility in the UI is not the same as server-side authorisation. Juice Shop documents missing access checks on privileged resources.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding based on the public Juice Shop challenge model. Architectural access-control flaws need dynamic review; this prototype flags the known training case rather than claiming full BAC coverage.
findings.recommendation: Enforce authorisation on every privileged API route. Deny by default, bind checks to the authenticated principal, and never trust hidden UI as a control.

findings.title: Authentication tokens use a weak or predictable signing configuration
findings.description: Session tokens are JWTs. In the training app, token integrity is not configured to production standards, which can let an attacker mint or alter claims if they learn the signing material.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. WebSET does not forge tokens.
findings.recommendation: Sign tokens with a strong algorithm and a high-entropy secret stored outside source control. Set short expiries, validate issuer/audience, and rotate keys.

findings.title: Sensitive configuration and comments leak from the client bundle
findings.description: Client-side code for the shop includes comments and configuration that reveal internals. Anything shipped to the browser is public, including secrets and internal URLs.
findings.evidence: Static catalog check: Juice Shop is designed to leave hints in client assets.
findings.recommendation: Keep secrets on the server. Strip comments and unused debug flags from production builds. Treat all frontend assets as untrusted public data.

findings.title: Missing or weak browser security headers
findings.description: Baseline header review looks for CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. Training apps often omit these.
findings.evidence: Live header inspection when the target is reachable; otherwise recorded from the demo catalog.
findings.recommendation: Set a restrictive CSP, nosniff, a framing policy, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy on every response. Prefer HTTPS with HSTS in non-lab environments.

findings.title: Component versions advertised in HTTP headers
findings.description: Response headers disclose runtime and framework names. Combined with a known-vulnerable training stack this raises the likelihood of using unpatched components.
findings.evidence: Header fingerprinting only. No vulnerability-exploit matching is performed.
findings.recommendation: Remove X-Powered-By and detailed Server banners. Track dependencies with a lockfile and a software composition process, and apply patches on a defined cadence.

findings.title: Login responses distinguish valid from invalid accounts
findings.description: Error text and timing can confirm whether an email is registered. That helps account enumeration.
findings.evidence: Catalog finding. WebSET does not brute-force credentials.
findings.recommendation: Return a single generic authentication failure message. Rate-limit login, and consider account lockout with user notification.

findings.title: Security-relevant events are not retained in a reviewable audit trail
findings.description: The training app does not provide an operator-facing audit stream for failed logins, authorisation failures, or input-validation failures.
findings.evidence: Catalog observation for the demo. Logging quality is not fully testable from an unauthenticated header check.
findings.recommendation: Log authentication, access-control, and validation failures with a correlation id. Protect logs from tampering and alert on repeated failures.

findings.title: Client-side integrity of third-party scripts is not enforced
findings.description: External scripts are loaded without Subresource Integrity. A compromised CDN could change shop behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Pin third-party scripts with SRI hashes, or self-host them. Use a CSP script-src allow-list.
